question: A 3-year-old child referred for genetic consultation to assess psychomotor retardation, language delay and hyperactivity without significant dysmorphic features or associated malformations. He is the first child of a healthy, young and non-consanguineous couple. A maternal uncle has mental retardation and the maternal grandmother presented early ovarian failure. Which of the following diagnostic tests would be the most appropriate to establish the diagnosis?

options.opa: Genetic study of triplet expansion of the FMR1 gene.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Psychomotor retardation" -> "Language delay" -> "Hyperactivity" -> "Family history of mental retardation" -> "Family history of early ovarian failure" -> "Possible Fragile X syndrome" -> "Genetic study of triplet expansion of the FMR1 gene" -> 95%

CHAIN: "Psychomotor retardation" -> "Language delay" -> "Hyperactivity" -> "No significant dysmorphic features" -> "Family history of mental retardation" -> "Consider genetic cause" -> "Genetic study of triplet expansion of the FMR1 gene" -> 90%

analysis: The clinical presentation of psychomotor retardation, language delay, and hyperactivity in a 3-year-old child, along with a family history of mental retardation in a maternal uncle and early ovarian failure in the maternal grandmother, is suggestive of Fragile X syndrome. This condition is caused by a triplet repeat expansion in the FMR1 gene. Therefore, the most appropriate diagnostic test is a genetic study of triplet expansion of the FMR1 gene.
